title: Strong Foundations, Strong Futures: Leadership Driving Education Reform Across Africa
author: Nomawethu Matshingana
excerpt: The education sector in South Africa and across the continent continues to experience important leadership-driven developments focused on strengthening systems, improving outcomes, and preparing institutions for future challenges.
body: The education sector in South Africa and across the continent continues to experience important leadership-driven developments focused on strengthening systems, improving outcomes, and preparing institutions for future challenges.

The Department of Basic Education (DBE), in partnership with Canva and other private sector partners, is preparing to host the 12th National Education Excellence Awards (NEEAs) on 24 July in Sandton. Under the theme "Strong Foundations, Strong Futures," the awards will recognise outstanding district leadership, operational excellence, and high-performing public schools across all quintiles from the 2025 National Senior Certificate (NSC) cycle. The event will bring together key education leaders, including Minister Siviwe Gwarube, Deputy Minister Dr Reginah Mhaule, and Director-General Mathanzima Mweli, to celebrate achievements within the public education system.

In higher education, Universities South Africa (USAf) and the Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) have shared key outcomes from the 2026 Entrepreneurial Executive Leadership Workshop. The discussions highlighted a growing shift among South Africa's 26 public universities towards embedding entrepreneurial thinking, innovation, and commercialisation into academic programmes. Rather than relying only on policy frameworks, university leaders are focusing on creating practical pathways that enable students and researchers to transform intellectual property and innovative ideas into market-ready solutions through stronger partnerships with industry.

Across Africa and globally, there is increasing recognition that effective school leadership is a specialised professional discipline and a vital driver of education transformation. The African Centre for School Leadership (ACSL) recently presented evidence at UNESCO IIEP's Strategic Debate, reinforcing the need to develop dedicated leadership pathways for school leaders beyond traditional teaching roles. This aligns with commitments by African education ministers to strengthen leadership development as a foundation for improving education systems. At UNESCO's global education discussions in Paris, President Cyril Ramaphosa also called for greater investment in foundational education and institutional capacity to ensure sustainable progress for future generations.
